newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Algerian president departs Bahrain after talks.
newsitem.headline: Algerian president departs Bahrain after talks.

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual on Wednesday left Bahrain after his country and the Gulf Arab state agreed to join forces in fighting political violence, the offical Gulf News Agency reported.
"There will be coordination between Bahrain and Algeria to wipe out terrorism from the Arab world," it quoted Zeroual as saying earlier in the day after talks with Bahraini officials.
Zeroual urged the Arab world to mobilise to fight "terrorism", saying Algeria felt the impact of "this dangerous phenomenon and its effects on other Arab and Islamic countries".
At least 50,000 people have been killed in Algeria since violence erupted after the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
In Bahrain, about 27 people have been killed, including three policemen and seven Bangladeshis, since anti-government protests broke out in December 1994 by members of the Shi'ite Moslem community.
Zeroual said that Bahrain and Algeria would set up a joint committee to promote cooperation in economic, trade, political and investment fields.
He arrived in Bahrain on Tuesday night on the first visit by an Algerian leader to the island state.
Zeroual was due to travel to China on Thursday for a five-day visit and then head to Vietnam. He is due to visit Qatar on his way back to Algeria.
